title: Zephyr Analytics - Discovery - Migration OpenAI to Dedicated
next_steps: Send Dedicated pricing deck and example contract
Share security whitepaper and SOC2 report
Schedule 1-hour technical deep dive with infra team next week
Run a 24-48h benchmark with Zephyr prompt set on Dedicated / vLLM parity tests
action_items: Lena Park: Send pricing estimates and Dedicated deployment options by 2025-12-05
Marcus Kim: Prep test harness, example eval scripts, and benchmark template by 2025-12-08
Carlos Ruiz: Share current prompt set (top 200) and traffic profile (QPS & seq length) by 2025-12-06
summary: Intro discovery for migrating Zephyr's production inference from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Main concerns: model/response parity, latency & cost tradeoffs, compatibility with vLLM/TGI stacks, network/VPC and KMS, SOC2/compliance. Agreed to run bench parity tests and schedule technical deep dive.
transcript:
Header: 2025-12-03 15:00 PST | Duration: 49m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Kim (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Head of ML - Zephyr), Carlos Ruiz (Infra), Aisha Khan (CTO)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on. really appreciate you making time. quick round robin — nina, do you want to kick off with your goals for the call?
[00:18] Nina Patel: yeah thanks lena. um so short version we run Zephyr's QA assistant and a bunch of analytics pipelines currently on OpenAI's API. we're hitting cost and variability issues as traffic scales and looking at dedicated or private options. main goals today: understand redwood dedicated vs hosted vs private, compatibility with our current OpenAI prompts and whether responses will be parity, and what infra work we'd need.
[00:43] Lena Park: perfect, that’s exactly what we usually cover. marcus from our se team will cover the technical bits, i'll handle pricing/contract and the rollout path.
[00:52] Marcus Kim: hi all, quick hello. i'll focus on latency, kv cache and batching implications, and how we integrate with existing vLLM/TGI setups if you have them.
[01:04] Aisha Khan: quick note from infra side — we need to know about VPC, private endpoints, and KMS for encryption. SOC2 is a must.
[01:12] Lena Park: absolutely, we can share SOC2 and our security whitepaper.
[01:16] Carlos Ruiz: for context we use a hybrid: some internal inference runs on vLLM in our k8s clusters for low-latency internal queries, and the customer-facing traffic is routed through OpenAI. we're prototyping TGI for some models. many of our prompts rely on system messages, tool-call style patterns, and streaming.
[01:38] Marcus Kim: ok good — that maps to lots of customers. question on parity: when you say parity do you mean exact token-for-token match or semantic equivalence and pass rate on your evals?
[01:49] Nina Patel: the latter mostly — we have eval pass rates and a few golden prompts that need to match behavior within tolerance. some endpoints are stricter — e.g. financial QA where hallucination is unacceptable.
[02:03] Marcus Kim: makes sense. operationally we see two classes of issues: model mismatch (architecture differences) and runtime/config differences (temperature, tokenization, stopping, function-calling behaviors). we typically do an eval harness that runs same prompt set across OpenAI model and our hosted/dedicated candidate and then measure pass/fail and delta on latency and cost.
[02:27] Lena Park: and for customers moving from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated we have a migration playbook — includes a parity benchmark, a canary rollout and fallbacks to hosted in case of regressions.
[02:38] [02:38] Nina Patel: what's the compatibility story for the API? we have a big codebase assuming OpenAI SDK names and function calling.
[02:46] Marcus Kim: Redwood's API is intentionally compatible — we support the same call shapes: completion/chat, function calling patterns, streaming and chunked responses. tiny differences appear in model naming (we provide model mapping docs) and in some edge cases around function calling errors. most customers wrap a thin adapter layer but many swap a base URL and key and are good to go.
[03:08] Carlos Ruiz: and for vLLM/TGI — if we want to run parts in-house and parts on redwood dedicated what does that look like?
[03:16] Marcus Kim: you can do hybrid routing. Redwood supports smart routing policies; you can route low-latency internal traffic to your vLLM infra and customer traffic to Dedicated, or vice versa. also we can run benchmarks to validate that redwood dedicated yields similar latencies to your vLLM setup.
[03:31] Aisha Khan: any differences with streaming? we've had issues where some libs chunk differently and client libraries couldn't reassemble reponse easily.
[03:39] Marcus Kim: streaming is supported; chunk boundaries can differ because of runtime internal tokenization/batching. if your client expects exact chunk sizes we can simulate with our streaming options. most integrations handle reassembly but we keep chunking as small as possible for low-latency.
[03:56] Nina Patel: pricing — we need ballpark cost for our current QPS. today we pay about $35k/mo to OpenAI for inference across a couple models, peak QPS around 120, average seq length ~600 tokens. monthly generation tokens ~150M.
[04:14] Lena Park: ok that's helpful. i'll follow up with a cost model for Dedicated vs hosted with estimated savings from batching and kv caching. usually Dedicated is a fixed capacity commit so you trade off predictable cost for lower per-token price.
[04:28] [04:28] Carlos Ruiz: is there an uplift for private/VPC installs? what about support SLAs?
[04:34] Lena Park: Private has platform fee plus support tiers; dedicated has SLA options for uptime/latency. we'll include that in the deck.
[04:41] Marcus Kim: on the technical side — can you share your latency SLOs? we want to match them in the benchmark.
[04:46] Nina Patel: customer-facing chat needs p99 < 500ms for short prompts and p95 < 1s for complex chains. internal tooling can tolerate higher latency.
[04:56] Marcus Kim: good target. we can tune batching windows, kv cache hit rates and use smaller model variants for certain routes to hit those p99s.
[05:06] Nina Patel: about model selection — we use GPT-4 style for critical tasks and GPT-3.5-ish for lower tier. do you support equivalent open models?
[05:15] Marcus Kim: we host a catalog of open model variants and also work with customers on custom weights. model behavior can differ; that's why the eval run is important. we also provide quantization profiles and kernel selection to reduce cost while preserving quality.
[05:30] [05:30] Aisha Khan: security: how do you manage keys and data at rest? we need KMS/HSM integration, logging and ability to purge customer data.
[05:40] Lena Park: we integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated; data retention is configurable and we provide audit logs and SIEM hooks. SOC2 report available.
[05:52] Carlos Ruiz: what about data in flight in a hybrid routing? is traffic proxied through your control plane?
[06:00] Marcus Kim: traffic routing options: for Dedicated we provide private peering and private endpoints, you can keep traffic inside your VPC for Private deployments. For hosted there's TLS and strict contractual terms but some customers prefer dedicated/private for sensitive data.
[06:14] Nina Patel: back to parity — how do you measure semantic drift? our evals are a mix of unit tests and human labels.
[06:23] Marcus Kim: we run both automated diff tests and human-in-the-loop checks on a subset. for hallucination we compute precision/recall of factual answers and have a regression alerting system tied to prompts. we'll share the eval harness.
[06:36] [06:36] Nina Patel: any customers moved from OpenAI to Dedicated and ran into nasty regressions?
[06:43] Lena Park: a few, mostly due to default temperature/tokenization differences. our playbook has a remediation flow: tweak sampling/stop tokens, try model variant, or fall back to hosted if rollback required.
[06:56] Carlos Ruiz: curious about latency tail from batching. some vendors' batching increases p99 under load.
[07:03] Marcus Kim: yes it's a key tradeoff. Redwood's runtime uses continuous batching + dynamic batching thresholds based on SLO. you can set max batching latency; we typically hit lower p99s than naive batching since we prioritize p99 slices and use prefix caching to avoid recomputation.
[07:21] Nina Patel: what's the typical integration timeline and effort?
[07:25] Lena Park: for a standard migration with parity benchmarks and canary rollout it's usually 6-12 weeks: week 1-2 discovery & eval dataset, week 3-4 bench runs and tuning, week 5-6 canary, then full rollout. Private/on-prem can take longer depending on approvals.
[07:42] Aisha Khan: do you support SAML/SSO and RBAC for console access?
[07:46] Lena Park: yes SAML, SSO, SCIM and role-based access control are supported.
[07:50] [07:50] Nina Patel: can we get a POC rather than full Dedicated commitment first? we have procurement constraints.
[07:57] Lena Park: we do pilot options: short-term reserved capacity or a usage-backed pilot with a commitment threshold. we can tailor that.
[08:06] Marcus Kim: i'll propose a test matrix: run your top 200 prompts across (1) OpenAI baseline (2) Redwood Hosted (3) Redwood Dedicated (4) your vLLM/TGI internal run. measure pass rate, latency distribution, and cost per 1k tokens.
[08:25] Carlos Ruiz: that matrix sounds perfect. also curious about model weights — can we bring our own weights to Dedicated?
[08:32] Marcus Kim: yes for Dedicated and Private we support customer-supplied weights subject to compatibility and licensing checks.
[08:38] [08:38] Nina Patel: about function calling — we've had differences in how some vendors return structured JSON vs stringified JSON. will that affect us?
[08:48] Marcus Kim: function calling behavior is generally the same but nuances exist in error responses and retry semantics. we will include function-calling tests in the harness.
[08:58] Lena Park: quick check — on procurement timeline where are you?
[09:02] Aisha Khan: we're hoping to decide on a path by EOY and start a pilot in January, full migration H1. procurement will need SOW and security docs.
[09:12] Lena Park: good — we'll prioritize SOC2, PCI notes, and a contract example in the followup.
[09:19] [09:19] Nina Patel: are there things we should be worried about when comparing outputs across runtimes? tokenizer differences were a surprise for us before.
[09:26] Marcus Kim: tokenizers can shift stop sequences and length counts — we recommend normalizing tokenization or adding a thin adapter in front that handles stop/trim rules. also set deterministic seeds for redo tests.
[09:38] Carlos Ruiz: do you offer a benchmark harness or code repo?
[09:42] Marcus Kim: yes we will share our benchmark harness (python scripts + docker) and an eval sheet.
[09:47] [09:47] Nina Patel: any limits on model versions we can pin? we need stable versioning for reproducibility.
[09:53] Lena Park: Dedicated supports model pinning and rollout policies (canary/AB) through the console and API.
[10:01] Marcus Kim: i'll also note quantization: we can run int8/4 quant profiles on Dedicated to cut cost; some tasks see no quality drop, others do. testing is needed.
[10:11] Aisha Khan: back to network — how do you handle peering setup? we need diagrams for networking to show our security team.
[10:18] Lena Park: we'll send a network diagram and a private peering checklist.
[10:22] [10:22] Nina Patel: let's talk about a concrete next step — run the benchmark, if parity is within acceptable delta proceed to pilot.
[10:28] Lena Park: agreed. action items: lena send pricing/security, marcus send harness, carlos share prompts/traffic. we'll target the benchmark to start by 12/09.
[10:38] Carlos Ruiz: one more: how to handle secrets rotation for service tokens in dedicated?
[10:43] Marcus Kim: Dedicated supports short-lived tokens, KMS integration and you can rotate keys via our console or API.
[10:49] [10:49] Aisha Khan: ok thanks everyone, i'll coordinate procurement timeline internally.
[10:53] Lena Park: thanks for the context — we'll follow up with the deck and docs. any last questions?
[10:58] Nina Patel: none from me. thanks.
[11:00] Lena Park: great, we'll send the followup by friday. bye all.

Notes: occasional transcription glitches: 'kv cache' heard as 'kay vee cache' in one spot; 'TGI' was mis-typed as 'T G I' by auto-gen. References shared: link: /sheets/zephyr-parity-template, link: /docs/redwood-security-whitepaper.pdf.
